note: Demo listings. The venue directory (data/venues.json) is baked from OpenStreetMap by scripts/build-venues.js — real places, real coordinates. This file is the editorial layer: events, offers, blurbs, tags and menus. Events, offers, menus, times and prices are illustrative examples, clearly badged as demo listings in the UI. See DATA.md.

church-inn.blurb: Hilltop pub beside St Chad's, brewing its own ales in the yard. Home of the Saddleworth Morris Men and the starting point of the Rushcart festival.

cross-keys.blurb: Stone-flagged moorside local up the hill from the village, long famous for its folk nights and its welcome for walkers straight off the tops.

waggon-inn.blurb: Coaching inn on Uppermill High Street — hearty food, cask ales and live music at the heart of the village.

items.name: Hand-battered fish & chips
items.desc: mushy peas, curry sauce on the side

items.name: Waggon burger
items.desc: smoked cheddar, burger sauce, skin-on fries

commie.blurb: The Commercial — 'the Commie' to everyone — a friendly boozer at the top end of the High Street with a busy calendar of open mics and beer festivals.

hare-and-hounds.blurb: Traditional stone pub on the High Street corner — proper pints, sport on the telly and a fireside seat in winter.

saddleworth-museum.blurb: The story of the Saddleworth villages — mills, moors, brass bands and the Rushcart — in an old mill beside the canal, with a gallery of local art.

uppermill-civic-hall.blurb: The village's big room — markets, fairs, concerts and community events all year round.

old-bell-inn.blurb: Eighteenth-century coaching inn holding a world-record gin collection behind its glowing gin emporium bar — plus rooms and a busy restaurant.

items.name: Gin-cured salmon
items.desc: cucumber, dill crème fraîche, rye crisp

items.name: Old Bell steak & juniper pie
items.desc: shortcrust, thick-cut chips, jug of gravy

items.name: Gin flight of three
items.desc: picked by the emporium team, paired tonics

items.name: Signature G&T of the week
items.desc: ask what's glowing on the wall

white-lion.blurb: Village pub in the heart of Delph, a stone's throw from the brook — quiz nights, cask ale and no airs and graces.

millgate-arts-centre.blurb: Saddleworth's little theatre — home of the Saddleworth Players, plus comedy, music and film nights through the year.

swan.blurb: Eighteenth-century pub on Dobcross Square, all low beams and stone floors — a favourite of brass banders on Whit Friday.

navigation-inn.blurb: Canalside pub by the old wool warehouse where the narrowboats once loaded — pints on the towpath in summer.

grandpa-greenes.blurb: Award-winning luxury ice cream served right on the canal towpath — deckchairs, ducks and sundaes with a view of the moors.

items.name: Flavour of the month
items.desc: ask at the hatch — it goes fast

items.name: The Standedge
items.desc: chocolate, honeycomb, fudge, a flake like a tunnel

items.name: Proper hot chocolate
items.desc: with or without a scoop dropped in

railway-inn.blurb: Opposite Greenfield station and the first pint off the Transpennine train — real ales, live music and a proper landlord's welcome.

king-william-iv.blurb: Friezland's local on the Oldham road — curry nights, quizzes and a beer garden under the hills.

boarshurst-band-club.blurb: Home of the Boarshurst Silver Band and the valley's Sunday-night brass concerts — visiting bands from across the North play here nearly every week.

saddleworth-cricket-bowling-and-tennis-c.blurb: The big sports club at Well-i-Hole — cricket on summer Saturdays, tennis courts and crown greens all season, and the valley's big bonfire and fireworks every November.

white-hart.blurb: Lydgate's celebrated dining pub on the brow of the hill — modern British cooking, a charcuterie of its own and views back across the whole of Saddleworth.

items.name: Herdwick lamb rump
items.desc: sheep's curd, wild garlic, hispi cabbage

items.name: Fish pie under a cheddar crust

rams-head-inn.blurb: A 400-year-old dining inn alone on the moor road above Denshaw, with its own farm shop and tea rooms next door.

items.name: Pan-roast pheasant breast
items.desc: smoked bacon, bread sauce, game jus

printers-arms.blurb: Denshaw's village pub — steak nights, cask ale and a warm room when the weather comes over the tops.

saddleworth-golf-club.blurb: A moorside course above the valley — every fairway has a view, and the 19th hole has an open fire. Visitors and societies welcome.

dovestone-sailing-club.blurb: Dinghies on Dovestone under Alderman and Alphin — one of the most dramatic places to sail in the North. Beginners' sessions all season.

three-crowns.blurb: High on the Oldham road at Scouthead with one of the best sunset views in the borough — beer festivals and big Sunday dinners.

farrars-arms.blurb: Roadside pub between Grasscroft and Lydgate with a sunny front terrace, acoustic sessions and a good line in Sunday lunches.

customVenues.name: The Royal Oak (Th'Heights)
customVenues.blurb: A candle-lit pub alone on the hillside above Delph, reached up a steep lane — worth every step for the view and the stew.

customVenues.name: The Diggle Hotel
customVenues.blurb: Stone free-house in the fold of the hills by the Standedge Tunnel end — pies, pints and trains rumbling under the moor.

items.name: Steak & Millstone ale
items.desc: with mash or chips, minted peas

customVenues.name: RSPB Dove Stone
customVenues.blurb: Moorland, woods and open water under the gritstone edges — peregrines and mountain hares up top, family trails around the reservoir. Car park and accessible paths at the bottom.

customVenues.name: Brownhill Countryside Centre
customVenues.blurb: Little canalside visitor centre at Brownhill Bridge — wildlife displays, family activities and the starting point for gentle towpath wanders.

customVenues.name: Castleshaw Roman Fort
customVenues.blurb: Grass-covered earthworks of a Roman fort guarding the pass over Standedge since AD 79, above the Castleshaw reservoirs. Always open, forever quiet.

customVenues.name: Dove Stone Reservoir Circular
customVenues.address: Start: Dovestone car park, Bank Lane, Greenfield
customVenues.blurb: The classic Saddleworth leg-stretcher: a flat, surfaced loop around the water with the gritstone edges towering over you. Pushchair and wheelchair friendly; herons guaranteed, ice cream van likely.

customVenues.name: Pots & Pans and the Obelisk
customVenues.blurb: Up through the lanes past St Chad's to the war memorial on Pots & Pans rock — the best view in the borough, from Winter Hill to Kinder on a clear day. Steep in places; earn your pint back at the Cross Keys.

customVenues.name: The Delph Donkey
customVenues.address: Start: Uppermill (or Delph — it works both ways)
customVenues.blurb: The old branch-line railway path from Uppermill to Delph, named after the train that once pottered along it. Flat, traffic-free and pram-friendly, with Dobcross on a hill above you all the way.

customVenues.name: Canal Towpath: Greenfield to Diggle
customVenues.address: Start: Well-i-Hole bridge, Greenfield (or any village on the way)
customVenues.blurb: The Huddersfield Narrow Canal through the whole valley — locks, herons, narrowboats and three villages' worth of pubs and cafés, ending at the mouth of the Standedge Tunnel. Grandpa Greene's is conveniently at the two-thirds mark.

customVenues.name: Standedge and the Boat Horse Road
customVenues.blurb: Follow the path the boat horses took over the moor while their narrowboats were legged through the tunnel beneath your feet. Wild, windy and wonderful — turn back at the cutting or carry on to Marsden and get the train home through the hill.

customVenues.name: Castleshaw Roman Fort Circular
customVenues.blurb: Out of Delph and up the Castleshaw valley to the Roman fort above the reservoirs — nineteen centuries of watching the pass, and still the best picnic spot in the north of the parish.

customVenues.name: Chew Valley to Chew Reservoir
customVenues.blurb: The steady climb up the old tramway road into the Chew Valley, between crags to the highest-built reservoir of its day in England. A proper lungful of Pennine air; boggy at the top after rain.

customVenues.name: Uppermill to Brownhill Riverside Loop
customVenues.blurb: The gentle family one: canal towpath out to the visitor centre at Brownhill Bridge, back along the Tame through the park. Ducks to feed, trains to wave at, and a playground finish.
